question: Does the frozen 0.25 direct-exit rule commit the never-consumed SC34 target while rejecting both new exact-target-absent cross-scene pairings without an unserved specialist request?

decision_rule.base_requirement: The unchanged local bilateral coherent-cycle and positive extent gates must commit.
decision_rule.direct_exit: Commit directly only when the primary local all-cycle fraction is at least 0.25.
decision_rule.ambiguous_branch: A local commit below 0.25 requests complementary corroboration. This frozen source has no active-query specialist, so any such request is explicitly unserved and non-committing.
decision_rule.composition: local AND primary-local-cycle >= 0.25; record but do not fabricate unavailable corroboration
decision_rule.threshold_authority: Inherited unchanged from l10-3rscan-selective-corroboration-cascade-posthoc-protocol-v1; no threshold sweep or repair is allowed.

forbidden_after_freeze: change the 0.25 threshold, local model, surface, frame, pair, cycle, component or extent gate
add an active query, global fit, retry or replacement after observing SC34
let positive query truth, target identity or reused FC31/FC08 decisions enter adjudication
claim a one-positive two-negative partial challenge is broad confirmation or measured early-exit speedup
claim_boundary: A pass is narrow scan-family-disjoint physical-target evidence for the fixed direct-exit decision on one new positive and two new exact-target-absent pairings. The negative query pixels were previously consumed for different targets, so only the SC34 referent/pairs are new. The carrier still uses privileged reference binding, same-provider geometry, desktop RoMa and SAM, and evaluates all branches before zero-model adjudication; it does not measure runtime savings or establish provider independence, arbitrary sibling rejection, raw-camera initial binding, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, deployment, user benefit, reliability or safety.
